title: Dev vs Prod
summary: Locking down a live app: moving secrets and settings (SECRET_KEY, the database password, ALLOWED_HOSTS, CORS allowed origins) into environment variables, closing the exposed database port, and moving the login token out of localStorage into an HttpOnly, Secure cookie. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Turn a working deployed app into a secured one by reading every secret from the environment and keeping the login token in an HttpOnly cookie.

steps.title: Run Django's deploy check
steps.detail: Read Django's deployment checklist, then run the built-in check on your practice project. It lists the dev-only settings this lecture fixes.
steps.doneWhen: You see a list of security warnings (DEBUG, SECRET_KEY, cookies and so on).

steps.title: Read MDN on cookies
steps.detail: Focus on the HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite attributes.
steps.doneWhen: You can explain why an HttpOnly cookie can't be stolen by an injected script but a localStorage token can.

steps.title: Confirm your Netflix secrets are ignored
steps.detail: Your Netflix .gitignore lists `.env` and `.env.local`. Check that git really ignores the file; you'll repeat this check on every project.
